\[
xyz = 3,
\]
\[
(x-y)(y-z)(z-x) = 4,
\]
\[
(x+y)(y+z)(z+x) = 40.
\]

Compute the minimum possible value for \( x \).

Give the minimum value of x as an exact expression using only integers, rational numbers, and radicals (no trigonometric or inverse trigonometric functions, and no approximations).

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

Let

\[
a=\frac yx,\qquad b=\frac zy,\qquad c=\frac xz.
\]

Then \(a,b,c>0\) and \(abc=1\). Also,

\[
(x-y)(y-z)(z-x)=xyz(1-a)(1-b)(1-c)=3(1-a)(1-b)(1-c),
\]

so

\[
(1-a)(1-b)(1-c)=\frac43.
\]

Similarly,

\[
(x+y)(y+z)(z+x)=xyz(1+a)(1+b)(1+c)=3(1+a)(1+b)(1+c),
\]

so

\[
(1+a)(1+b)(1+c)=\frac{40}{3}.
\]

Let \(S=a+b+c\) and \(P=ab+bc+ca\). Since \(abc=1\),

\[
(1+a)(1+b)(1+c)=S+P+2=\frac{40}{3},
\]
\[
(1-a)(1-b)(1-c)=P-S=\frac43.
\]

Solving gives

\[
S=5,\qquad P=\frac{19}{3}.
\]

Thus \(a,b,c\) are the roots of

\[
t^3-5t^2+\frac{19}{3}t-1=0.
\]

Factoring,

\[
t^3-5t^2+\frac{19}{3}t-1=(t-3)\left(t^2-2t+\frac13\right),
\]

so

\[
\{a,b,c\}=\left\{3,\;1+\sqrt{\frac23},\;1-\sqrt{\frac23}\right\}.
\]

Now \(y=ax\) and \(z=abx\), so

\[
xyz=a^2b x^3=3.
\]

Hence

\[
x^3=\frac{3}{a^2b}.
\]

Using \(abc=1\), we get

\[
x^3=\frac{3c}{a}.
\]

To minimize \(x\), we minimize \(x^3\). Among the three possible values of \(a\) and \(c\), the smallest value of \(\frac{3c}{a}\) occurs when \(c\) is the smallest root and \(a\) is the largest root:

\[
c=1-\sqrt{\frac23},\qquad a=3.
\]

This is valid because then \(b=1+\\sqrt{\frac23}\). Therefore

\[
x_{\min}^3=3\cdot \frac{1-\sqrt{2/3}}{3}=1-\sqrt{\frac23}.
\]

Thus the minimum possible value of \(x\) is

\[
\boxed{\sqrt[3]{1-\sqrt{\frac23}}}.
\]
